classification.difficultyReason: Independently link half an hour of travel to distance, interpret 280 degrees as north of west and select a trigonometric ratio for the northward component.

content.prompt: A car travels on a bearing of $280^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ on a very long straight road at $85\text{ km/h}$, starting from an initial point at 12 p.m. Find how far north the car is from its original point at 12:30 p.m., correct to one-tenth of a kilometre.

answer.worked:
The bearing is $10^{\circ}$ north of west, so the northward distance is opposite the $10^{\circ}$ angle.

$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{30}{60}=0.5\text{ h}\\d&=85\times0.5\\d&=42.5\text{ km}\\\theta&=280^{\circ}-270^{\circ}\\\theta&=10^{\circ}\\n&=42.5\sin10^{\circ}\\n&\approx7.4\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

The car is $7.4\text{ km}$ north of its original point.
